name: Langtang & Gosaikunda
tagline: Glacier valleys and sacred lakes near Kathmandu
meta_description: Langtang and Gosaikunda treks: Langtang Valley, Gosaikunda yatra, Helambu, Tamang Heritage Trail, Yala Peak and heli tours. Prices, seasons and permits.
summary: Langtang is the closest major trekking region to Kathmandu, a 6–7 hour drive to Syabrubesi. In a week you can walk to Kyanjin Gompa at 3,870 m below Langtang Lirung, or climb to the sacred Gosaikunda lake at 4,380 m. Best months are October–November and March–May; a Langtang National Park permit and licensed guide are required.
intro: Langtang rises directly north of Kathmandu, so close that on a clear morning you can see Langtang Lirung, 7,227 m, from the rooftops of Thamel. No flight is needed: a jeep reaches the trailhead at Syabrubesi in 6–7 hours, and by the third day of walking you are among yak pastures and glaciers near the Tibetan border. That short approach makes Langtang the best choice for travellers with 7–10 days who still want high mountains, and the least expensive of Nepal's big trekking regions.

The region holds three distinct treks. The Langtang Valley follows the Langtang Khola through forest home to red pandas and langur monkeys, past the rebuilt Langtang village, to Kyanjin Gompa at 3,870 m, where a cheese factory founded in 1955 still sells yak cheese. To the south-west, a steep trail climbs from Dhunche past Sing Gompa to Gosaikunda at 4,380 m, a lake sacred to Shiva. East of the lakes, Laurebina La at 4,610 m leads down into the Hyolmo villages of Helambu.

Most of the people here are Tamang, a Tibetan Buddhist community whose stone villages, carved wooden windows and mani walls line every route. The Tamang Heritage Trail links Gatlang, Tatopani hot springs and Nagthali in a gentle 7-day loop with homestays. In 2015 the earthquake triggered an avalanche that buried old Langtang village and destroyed most lodges up the valley. The valley has been rebuilt, and trekking income helps families who lost relatives and homes.

Langtang National Park, created in 1976, was Nepal's first Himalayan national park and covers about 1,710 km². Teahouses run along all the main trails, with simpler rooms than Everest or Annapurna but warm dining rooms and dal bhat at every stop. For those who cannot walk far, helicopters land at Kyanjin Gompa and beside Gosaikunda in 35–40 minutes from Kathmandu. Our packages include permits, licensed guides, porters, jeeps and meals, priced in INR and USD.

highlights.title: Kyanjin Gompa and Kyanjin Ri
highlights.text: Kyanjin Gompa, at 3,870 m, sits in a wide glacial basin below Langtang Lirung, 7,227 m. From here a 3–4 hour round trip climbs Kyanjin Ri, 4,773 m, for views over the glaciers, and strong walkers take a full day to Tserko Ri, 4,984 m. The small monastery and the yak cheese factory sit beside the lodges.

highlights.title: Gosaikunda, Shiva's lake
highlights.text: Gosaikunda lies at 4,380 m in a chain of more than a dozen lakes, a Ramsar wetland since 2007. Hindus believe Shiva created it with his trident to cool his throat after swallowing poison. It is reached in 3–4 days from Dhunche via Sing Gompa, or in about 35 minutes by helicopter from Kathmandu.

highlights.title: Janai Purnima pilgrimage
highlights.text: On the full moon of Janai Purnima, usually in August, thousands of Hindu pilgrims and jhankri shamans walk to Gosaikunda to bathe in the icy lake and renew the sacred thread. Tents and food stalls line the shore for two to three days, despite monsoon rain on the trail.

highlights.title: Langtang village, rebuilt
highlights.text: The 2015 avalanche buried old Langtang village under rock and ice. Survivors rebuilt a new village at 3,430 m a short way up the valley, with lodges, a gompa and a memorial chorten listing the dead. Staying here supports families who returned, and the walk across the debris field is a sobering moment.

highlights.title: Tamang Heritage Trail and Gatlang
highlights.text: Gatlang, at about 2,240 m, is a village of stone houses with carved windows and slate roofs where Tamang families host trekkers in homestays. The 7-day Tamang Heritage Trail adds natural hot springs at Tatopani and the Nagthali meadow, which faces Langtang Lirung and Ganesh Himal, without going higher than about 3,165 m.

highlights.title: Helambu and Laurebina La
highlights.text: Helambu is the land of the Hyolmo people, with monasteries at Tarkeghyang and Melamchi Gaon and apple orchards on terraced ridges. It can be walked in 5 days from Sundarijal, near Kathmandu, or joined to Gosaikunda over Laurebina La, 4,610 m, for a 13–14 day traverse ending close to the capital.

getting_there: Every Langtang trek starts by road from Kathmandu. A private jeep covers the 122 km to Syabrubesi in 6–7 hours via Trishuli Bazar, Betrawati and Dhunche, on a road that is paved in parts and rough and narrow above Betrawati; local buses leave Machhapokhari in Kathmandu early each morning and take 8–9 hours. Gosaikunda treks usually start at Dhunche, 1,960 m, about an hour before Syabrubesi. The Tamang Heritage Trail begins at Syabrubesi or Gatlang. Helambu and Chisapani treks start at Sundarijal, 45 minutes by car from Thamel, and finish by jeep from Melamchi, Timbu or Tarkeghyang in 4–6 hours. Helicopters fly from Tribhuvan Airport to Kyanjin Gompa in about 40 minutes and to Gosaikunda in about 35 minutes, in clear morning weather only.
permits: All trekkers need a Langtang National Park entry permit: NPR 3,000 for foreigners and NPR 1,500 for SAARC nationals, including Indians, sold in Kathmandu and at the Dhunche park office. A TIMS card is also required for foreign trekkers. Since April 2023, Nepal's rules require foreign trekkers to walk with a licensed guide booked through a registered agency, and the rule is checked on Langtang trails. Helambu routes from Sundarijal also pay the Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park fee of about NPR 1,000. Yala Peak needs an NMA climbing permit. No restricted area permit applies on the main routes. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Kyanjin Gompa −14 to 4 °C, Chisapani −2 to 12 °C, dry and clear
months.summary: January is the coldest month, with dry air and long clear views. The low treks are excellent: Chisapani and the Shivapuri hills face Langtang Lirung and Ganesh Himal, and Helambu's villages are sunny by day. The Langtang Valley is possible with good gear, but Kyanjin Gompa drops well below freezing at night and snow can block the trail above Langtang village. Gosaikunda is usually frozen and snowbound, and the route to Laurebina La is not advised.
months.tip: Pack a −15 °C sleeping bag for any January night above 3,000 m, as lodge rooms are unheated.

months.weather: Langtang village −8 to 8 °C, Gatlang −3 to 12 °C, cold, late snowfalls
months.summary: February remains cold, with occasional heavy snow higher up and clear spells between storms. Tamang villages celebrate Sonam Lhosar, the Tamang new year, in late January or February with dances, family feasts and prayer flags, a good reason to walk the Tamang Heritage Trail through Gatlang. Helambu and Chisapani are pleasant. The Langtang Valley is quiet and beautiful but cold, and lodges above Lama Hotel may be short-staffed early in the month.
months.tip: Ask your guide to time a February Tamang Heritage Trail to include Sonam Lhosar in Gatlang.

months.weather: Kyanjin Gompa −6 to 9 °C, Syabrubesi 9 to 22 °C, warming, afternoon cloud
months.summary: March opens the spring season. Rhododendrons begin to flower in the forests between Lama Hotel and Ghoda Tabela and around Sing Gompa, and the Langtang Valley warms day by day. Kyanjin Ri is usually clear of snow by mid-month. Gosaikunda remains frozen, and Laurebina La can still hold deep snow, so the full Gosaikunda and Helambu traverse is better from late March or April. Mornings are clear, with cloud building after midday.
months.tip: Start each March day by 7 am to see Langtang Lirung before cloud builds in the afternoon.

months.weather: Kyanjin Gompa −2 to 12 °C, Gosaikunda −6 to 7 °C, mild, some storms
months.summary: April is the best spring month in Langtang. Rhododendron forests are in full flower red and pink, temperatures at Kyanjin Gompa are comfortable by day and Gosaikunda begins to thaw at its edges. All three main treks, the valley, the lakes and Helambu, are open, and Yala Peak climbing season starts. Afternoon thunderstorms are possible, and views are best early in the day. Lodges are busy but never crowded like Everest.
months.tip: Carry a light rain shell in April for afternoon storms that can bring hail above 3,500 m.

months.weather: Kyanjin Gompa 2 to 15 °C, Syabrubesi 15 to 28 °C, warm, hazy
months.summary: May is warm and good at altitude, with Gosaikunda fully thawed and the yak herders moving up to summer pastures around Kyanjin. Haze and pre-monsoon cloud build through the month, so distant views are less sharp than in autumn. The lower forests are hot and humid below 2,000 m, and leeches appear on wet days late in May. It remains a good month for Yala Peak, Tserko Ri and the Gosaikunda and Helambu traverse.
months.tip: Finish May treks before the last week of the month, when the first monsoon storms often arrive.

months.weather: Syabrubesi 18 to 28 °C, Dhunche 15 to 24 °C, monsoon rain from mid-June
months.summary: The monsoon usually reaches Langtang in mid-June. Heavy rain falls on the forested lower valleys, leeches are common, rivers rise and landslides block the road between Betrawati and Syabrubesi. Cloud hides the peaks most days. We do not run regular treks in June. For a short outing near Kathmandu, the Shivapuri forest trails are walkable between showers, and Dhunche stays cooler than the capital.
months.tip: If you travel in June, allow a spare day for landslide delays on the Syabrubesi road.

months.weather: Syabrubesi 19 to 28 °C, Kyanjin Gompa 7 to 16 °C, wettest month
months.summary: July is the wettest month. Trails are muddy and slippery, leeches cling to every bush below 3,000 m, and road closures are frequent. Kyanjin Gompa is green and full of flowers but usually under cloud, and the walk in through the gorge is unpleasant. A few pilgrims begin preparing for the Gosaikunda full-moon walk. We advise trekkers to choose Upper Mustang or another rain-shadow route instead of Langtang this month.
months.tip: Carry salt, long socks and leech repellent on any July walk in the Langtang forests.

months.weather: Dhunche 15 to 24 °C, Gosaikunda 3 to 12 °C, rain, cloud and mist
months.summary: August is still monsoon, but it is the month of Janai Purnima, when thousands of pilgrims walk from Dhunche through Sing Gompa to Gosaikunda for the Shrawan full moon. The trail is crowded, wet and muddy, and temporary tents and stalls line the lakeshore for the festival. Pilgrims should be fit, carry rain gear and acclimatise at Chandanbari. Regular trekking is not advised, and the Langtang Valley road often suffers landslides.
months.tip: For Janai Purnima, start from Dhunche three days before the full moon and sleep a night at Chandanbari to acclimatise.

months.weather: Langtang village 6 to 16 °C, Syabrubesi 17 to 27 °C, rain easing
months.summary: September is a shoulder month. Rain eases through the month, landslide damage on the road is repaired and the valleys are lush and quiet. Early-September treks still meet showers and leeches below Lama Hotel, but by the last week views of Langtang Lirung return most mornings. It is a good time for the Tamang Heritage Trail and the Langtang Valley at lower prices before the October rush.
months.tip: Book departures after 20 September for the best chance of clear mornings and dry trails.

months.weather: Kyanjin Gompa −4 to 12 °C, Gosaikunda −7 to 8 °C, dry, very clear
months.summary: October is the peak month, with clear skies, dry trails and sharp views of Langtang Lirung, Ganesh Himal and the Annapurnas from Laurebina La. Every route is open, including the full Langtang, Gosaikunda and Helambu traverse and Yala Peak. Dashain and Tihar holidays bring Nepali trekkers too, so lodges at Kyanjin Gompa and Gosaikunda fill on some nights. Nights are frosty above 3,500 m.
months.tip: Book jeeps to Syabrubesi early for Dashain week in October, when vehicles are scarce.

months.weather: Kyanjin Gompa −8 to 9 °C, Helambu 1 to 14 °C, dry, cold nights
months.summary: November gives some of the clearest air of the year, with fewer trekkers than October. The Langtang Valley is excellent, though Kyanjin Gompa drops well below freezing at night. Gosaikunda starts to freeze over by late November, and an early snowfall can make Laurebina La icy, so carry microspikes on the traverse. The Tamang Heritage Trail and Helambu are at their best, with harvested fields and long sunny days.
months.tip: Bring microspikes for Laurebina La in late November, when the first snow often freezes on the trail.

months.weather: Kyanjin Gompa −12 to 6 °C, Chisapani 0 to 14 °C, dry, clear, cold
months.summary: December is dry, cold and quiet. The Langtang Valley is still trekkable with a warm sleeping bag, and the views from Kyanjin Ri are crisp, but lodge owners above Langtang village thin out and some close. Gosaikunda is frozen and often snowbound, and we do not cross Laurebina La in December. The lower treks, Chisapani, Helambu and the Shivapuri ridge, are at their best for short breaks from Kathmandu.
months.tip: Choose the 3-day Chisapani and Nagarkot walk for a December short break with mountain views and warmer nights.

faqs.q: How many days is the Langtang Valley trek?
faqs.a: Usually 7–8 days from Kathmandu: a day's drive to Syabrubesi, three days walking up via Lama Hotel and Langtang village to Kyanjin Gompa, a day to climb Kyanjin Ri, two days back down and the drive out. Our 8-day package starts from ₹58,000 or US$ 690. Fast walkers can do it in 6 days.

faqs.q: What is the Langtang trek cost?
faqs.a: Our packages start from about ₹58,000 or US$ 690 for the 8-day Langtang Valley trek, ₹75,000 or US$ 890 for 11 days with Gosaikunda and ₹92,000 or US$ 1,090 for 14 days with Helambu, per person on twin sharing. Prices include the private jeep, licensed guide, porters, permits, teahouses and three meals a day on the trail.

faqs.q: Is the Langtang trek good for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes. The Langtang Valley is one of the best first treks in Nepal, with 5–7 hours of walking a day and a top sleeping altitude of 3,870 m at Kyanjin Gompa. It needs reasonable fitness for long climbs through forest. Gosaikunda is harder, gaining height quickly from Dhunche, and the Laurebina La traverse suits trekkers with some experience.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for the Langtang trek?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are a foreign national. Since April 2023 Nepal's rules require foreign trekkers in national parks to walk with a licensed guide arranged through a registered agency, and checkpoints at Dhunche and Syabrubesi check this. You also need the Langtang National Park permit and a TIMS card. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I get from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi?
faqs.a: By road: about 122 km, taking 6–7 hours by private jeep or 8–9 hours by local bus from Machhapokhari bus park. The road passes Trishuli Bazar, Betrawati and Dhunche and is rough above Betrawati. Our packages include a private jeep. A helicopter takes about 30 minutes but is rarely used for the trailhead.

faqs.q: Can I combine Langtang Valley and Gosaikunda?
faqs.a: Yes. After Kyanjin Gompa, walk back to Thulo Syabru and climb via Sing Gompa to Gosaikunda, then exit to Dhunche. This takes 11 days from Kathmandu and starts from ₹75,000 or US$ 890. Adding Laurebina La and Helambu makes a 14-day traverse that finishes by jeep from Tarkeghyang.

faqs.q: What is the Gosaikunda helicopter tour price?
faqs.a: Our Gosaikunda heli yatra from Kathmandu starts from ₹58,000 or US$ 690 per seat when shared, with about 35 minutes of flying each way and a short stop at 4,380 m for darshan. Flights run in clear morning weather only. People with heart or lung disease and pregnant women should not fly to this altitude.

faqs.q: Is Langtang safe after the 2015 earthquake?
faqs.a: Yes, the trails and lodges were rebuilt in the years after 2015, and the valley has received trekkers every season since. Landslide risk remains in the monsoon, so we do not run treks from June to August. In spring and autumn the route is stable, and guides keep in touch with lodges about conditions.

faqs.q: When is the best time for the Gosaikunda yatra?
faqs.a: For trekking, October–November and April–May give dry trails and clear views of the lakes. Pilgrims often go for Janai Purnima, the Shrawan full moon in August, when thousands bathe in the lake; it is crowded and wet but spiritually important. Our 7-day Janai Purnima pilgrimage trek starts from ₹36,000 or US$ 430.
